sections.title: Article V: the states’ way to fix Congress
How it works
notes: state legislatures (two-thirds of 50) apply. Congress “shall call” a convention.
states (three-fourths) must ratify any amendment it proposes, by legislature or state convention.

notes: Georgia Alaska Florida Alabama Tennessee Indiana Oklahoma Louisiana Arizona North Dakota Texas Missouri Arkansas Utah Mississippi Wisconsin Nebraska West Virginia South Carolina Kansas
The 20 states and their official records

Dates are the advocacy group’s. “Official record” is the state’s application as received by the U.S. House Clerk (or, where the Clerk’s list has no copy, the state legislature’s record), read by us for the Convention of States wording (“impose fiscal restraints … limit the power and jurisdiction of the federal government … limit the terms of office”). Blank means we have not yet linked an official copy; the state stays in the group’s count, not ours.
The owner, in the owner’s words

Members of Congress are bound by their oath and the Constitution to represent the people. Both parties took control from the people while ordinary Americans were busy caring for their families. We the people own and operate this country. Another election just puts more people in to do the same thing. An Article V convention of states is the only way to change Congress.

article-v-1.title: The Congress, whenever two thirds of both Houses shall deem it necessary, shall propose Amendments to this Constitution, or, on…
lines: The Congress, whenever two thirds of both Houses shall deem it necessary, shall propose Amendments to this Constitution, or, on the Application of the Legislatures of two thirds of the several States, shall call a Convention for proposing Amendments, which, in either Case, shall be valid to all Intents and Purposes, as Part of this Constitution, when ratified by the Legislatures of three fourths of the several States, or by Conventions in three fourths thereof, as the one or the other Mode of Ratification may be proposed by the Congress; Provided that no Amendment which may be made prior to the Year One thousand eight hundred and eight shall in any Manner affect the first and fourth Clauses in the Ninth Section of the first Article; and that no State, without its Consent, shall be deprived of its equal Suffrage in the Senate.
U.S. Constitution, Article V
